claim: DKS collapsed FL's Spanish European holding company (Foot Locker Europe Holdings SLU, Barcelona) into Foot Locker Dutch Holdings B.V. by an intra-EU cross-border merger. Draft terms were signed 2026-03-20 and the Spanish entity's dissolution by merger was registered 2026-08-28. INFERENCE: a single Dutch holding stack makes a later carve-out, sale or licence transfer simpler, but the step is equally consistent with routine post-deal tax and entity clean-up. The filings mention no sale.
data_point: The Spanish European holdco (CIF B85826006) was eliminated, so the European holding chain now sits in a Dutch B.V. Neither entity has employees. Dates: draft terms 2026-03-20; deposited at the Barcelona registry 2026-04-15; sole-shareholder approval 2026-05-18; Dutch GM approval (unanimous) 2026-06-16; notice signed 2026-06-18 by Larisa Love Chaleff; BORME-A 2026-09-07 #405010 'Disolucion. Fusion (28.08.26)'.

Closed in 2025 (list comparison): one of two Liege stores, Namur, Hasselt. Belgian net revenue EUR 39.04M -> 31.08M (-20.4%); Luxembourg EUR 16.24M -> 14.61M (-10.0%). Consolidating parent: Dick's Sporting Goods, Inc. (Coraopolis). The directors' report says no circumstances could materially affect the company's development. The board proposes paying the Luxembourg branch's distributable reserves up to the Belgian head office.

The BE+LU fleet of 20 stores is about 3.6% of FL Europe's 559, so the pace may not generalise. Not in KNOWN_BRIEF, the baseline or other confirmed files.

claim: FL Germany's lease book is short. claim: Bottom-up store-level reconstruction for 8 FL Europe locator countries (DE, NL, BE, PL, CZ, AT, LU, HU; about 27-29% of FL Europe). Corrected live census on 2026-10-07: 153 listed stores (DE 78, NL 22, BE 15, PL 12, CZ 10, AT 6, LU 6, HU 4), of which about 150 are actually trading. In the window from the deal close to now there were about 14-17 gross closures and 2-3 openings, a net of about -11 to -15 on about 165 stores (-7% to -9% in 13 months, roughly 6.5-8% a year). That compares with a benchmark of about 4% a year for Europe as a whole (581 to 559) and a flat Bloomberg consensus. At least 10-12 of the closures carry post-FYE (after 2026-01-31) evidence, which works out to at least about 9% a year gross in this sample.
data_point: Live 2026-10-07: 153 listed (DE78 NL22 BE15 PL12 CZ10 AT6 LU6 HU4); ~150 trading after excluding 3 stale listings. That is REFUTED: a Google review dated 2025-06-17 says 'Der Laden ist leer' (the store is empty), so it closed before the deal. The Berlin city page kept a stale card through 2025-10-07, which I verified in Wayback captures 20250323, 20250712 and 20251007 (card present) and 20260120 (gone). This shows that locator 'last-listed' dates can lag real closures by months. (2) The 3 listed-but-closed stores all closed before the deal or have undated windows: Recklinghausen Palais Vest (Google review 2025-01-11 says the shop no longer exists, matching the CY2024 Recklinghausen closure in the FL Germany accounts), Liege Vinave d'Ile (Google says closed 2023-12; Sudinfo 2023), and Liege Belle-Ile (closure window 2025-04-18 to 2026-08-27). They show the locator overstates trading stores, not that closures accelerated. (3) Hoofddorp's last Google review is 2025-02-01, so its timing is uncertain. (4) The live census is CONFIRMED: Budapest city page shows 13802/13803/13804/13807, and Brno lists Vankovka #13413. The west-census confirmed file put HU at 3 and CZ at 9 because its sitemap regex missed the malformed fids (13803 '550_ 31_13803', 13413), so HU=4 and CZ=10 is the correct count. (5) Most individual closures in this list already appear in D_w1_landlords-malls, D_w1_gmaps-closed, D_w1_chatter and C_w1_labor-rest. The novel part is this 8-country net time series and run-rate. Inference: since Europe reported only -14 net from FYE to 8/1/26, the at least 10-12 post-FYE closures in this ~29% sample point either to gross Europe closures well above the net figure or to closures continuing into Q3 FY26. Vaci u. 14 still had normal Google reviews on 2026-09-21 (per D_w1_gmaps-closed), which points to a Q3 FY26 closure.
